items.label: A
items.critique: Punchy and plain, but the opener packs cause, history and who-to-ask into one tidy briefing, and the 'into the fire with you' bark is a writer's flourish. Generic title ('Guildmaster') in place of a masked name.

items.label: B
items.critique: The cells threat and the formal release line are close to Nox, but 'home of the bravest garrison in the realm' plus the blocked-road-and-who-decides formula reads assembled to spec.

items.label: C
items.critique: Same three-beat block (danger, consequence, who barred it, ask them) as other new texts; 'keep to the planks' is neat but the whole set is too economical and evenly paced.

items.label: D
items.critique: Breathless, slightly clumsy urgency ('You have arrived! Lives are at stake!'), redundant repetition in the reminder and the stock 'Your valor knows no peer' are pure Westwood.

items.label: E
items.critique: Dry officious humour (no spitting, don't even think about wizardry), 'Oh, I forgot to mention' and the trailing 'huh...' are Nox's comic guard voice.

items.label: F
items.critique: Stiff, slightly preachy register ('for the common man'), bare 'Move on!' and the masked name in the first line match the campaign's gate guards.

items.label: G
items.critique: Flat, minimal, no quest pointer, page break mid-welcome and an escalating 'Last warning' that leads nowhere: the unpolished filler of the original.

items.label: H
items.critique: Inn welcome stapled to a barred-road briefing with 'ask her inside', and a drunk-guard 'Hiccup!' gag that feels inserted to tick a humour box.

items.label: I
items.critique: Proud, stilted civic lines with a grammar slip ('can be dangerous place') and no instruction at all; nobody writing to spec would leave it this loose.

items.label: J
items.critique: Again sealed-area, monster, only-X-can-open, find-him-by-Y; the later line borrows Westwood's 'brave Adventurer' but the whole is too neatly symmetrical.

tells: New guards all deliver the same three-beat briefing in the first line: what is closed, which monster caused it, which titled NPC decides and where to find him. Westwood's guards often point nowhere, or only welcome and threaten.
New texts use generic titles (the Captain, the Foreman, the Elder, the Guildmaster) where Westwood uses a proper name (masked [Person]/[Place]/[Class]).
New sentences are uniformly short and clean; Westwood's are uneven, with redundant repetition, stock praise ('Your valor knows no peer'), grammar slips and stiff officialese.
Humour in new texts is a bolted-on gag (hiccups, 'mind your head'); Westwood's humour comes from the guard's own pompous or bored character.
The 'later' line in new texts always closes the loop neatly (road open, safe travels); Westwood's can be a non sequitur or an escalation.
